distribution.title: Student's t-distribution
distribution.intro: The t-distribution with \(\nu>0\) degrees of freedom is symmetric around zero and has heavier tails than the standard normal distribution.

The mean is zero for \(

u/(

distribution.course: The course uses a t distribution with n−1 degrees of freedom for a confidence interval for a normal mean when the variance is unknown.
distribution.course_link: Build a confidence interval with unknown variance
distribution.r_intro: These examples use functions from R’s stats package. For functions with d, p, q, and r prefixes, they compute a density or mass, cumulative probability, quantile, and random samples, respectively.
